title: Bidirectional Dijkstra: Reykjavík Route Lightning
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra shrink the search space by expanding shortest-path frontiers from both the start and the goal. On a real street-graph, it meets in the middle and reconstructs the optimal path efficiently.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Reykjavík streets meet serious graph theory!

In this visualization, **Bidirectional Dijkstra** runs two coordinated Dijkstra searches: one from the **start** node and one from the **goal** node. Each direction maintains its own **priority queue** and **distance map**, expanding nodes in increasing cost order until the two frontiers **meet** at a best candidate overlap. ✅

📌 Why it’s fast on real maps: your street network is a weighted graph (edges = road segments, weights = distance/time). By searching from both ends, it often avoids exploring large portions of the graph that a single-source Dijkstra would touch—especially when the shortest path isn’t near-uniform across the whole network.

🔍 The algorithmic moment to notice: the stopping condition relies on the **current best path cost** from forward+backward exploration, letting the run terminate as soon as no unseen node can improve the solution.

✅ Stop early when the optimal meet point is guaranteed
